paragraphs: ReturnRing helps a fashion e-commerce choose and explain the best action on every return, within EU consumer law. Statistical models estimate return probability, abuse risk, customer value and product anomalies; a rules engine picks the admissible actions; a simulator estimates their net benefit under explicit assumptions; Gemma 4 explains each decision and drafts the customer message, through AMD Token Factory (or a local vLLM, optional). A person approves every restrictive action.

Built for the AMD Developer Hackathon ACT III (lablab.ai), Track 3 "Reinvent Commerce". The full specification is docs/spec.md (in Italian); the decisions are in docs/adr/; the current delivery scope is ADR-18.

How to read the numbers. Every figure in this README names its origin, its period and its nature: real (measured on real data or real hardware), synthetic (measured on the generated store, whose abuse behaviours are design hypotheses) or simulated (computed under stated assumptions). The demo's golden cases are demo cases, never a measure of accuracy.
